description:
AETHER X is an advanced, zero-setup web observatory designed to bridge complex astrophysical data and public participation for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. The platform transforms NASA’s SPHEREx all-sky spectral survey into an intuitive browser-based discovery laboratory, empowering students, researchers, and citizen scientists to actively assist in the hunt for the hypothesized Planet X (Ninth Planet) and other trans-Neptunian objects.

Created by Almira Baloğlu.

details:
AETHER X is an advanced, zero-setup digital observatory prepared for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. The core purpose of the project is to make complex space data and astrophysical analysis understandable, interactive, and accessible to everyone.

What Does the Project Do and How Does It Work?

AETHER X integrates NASA's SPHEREx all-sky survey data, WISEview time-series archives, ESA Gaia astrometry catalogs, and CADC/NEOSSat orbital telemetry into a single screen. The system is built upon two main pillars:

  1. Multi-Epoch Image Comparison (Wiseview Blink): It allows you to superimpose historical archive photographs with current SPHEREx scans, using transparency controls or an automatic blinking mode to instantly spot moving objects among stationary stars.
  2. 102-Band Infrared Spectrum Analysis: It enables you to examine methane absorption lines found in cold brown dwarfs and planets through live charts, utilizing 102 distinct infrared wavelength channels provided by SPHEREx.

What Are the Benefits and Intended Impact?

Studying traditional space data requires heavy desktop software or advanced programming knowledge. AETHER X removes this barrier, enabling students, researchers, and citizen scientists to directly participate in space exploration. The primary goal of the project is to accelerate the discovery of mysterious outer Solar System bodies and the hypothesized Planet X (Ninth Planet), while supporting NASA's Open Science philosophy.

What Tools and Technologies Were Used?

The project was developed in a single-file architectural structure using modern web technologies (HTML5, CSS3/Tailwind CSS, and interactive HTML5 Canvas rendering engines) to ensure maximum performance and portability. It runs directly within the browser without requiring any server load.

Project Creativity and Team Factors:

Almira Baloğlu, the leader of the "Open Data Solo" team and the architect of the project, is a passionate high school student whose dreams always reach for the high skies and who aims to become a software and data engineer. While designing AETHER X, user experience was prioritized, incorporating both guided discovery tours for beginners and advanced features like JPL asteroid vetting and JSON scientific data export for professionals.
